topic: Public monitoring adds triage, validity, API, and webhooks
caption:
GitHub public monitoring now enables programmatic alert management, but closing an alert does not automatically revoke the exposed credential.

Enterprise security teams managing leaked secrets in public repositories often struggle with noise and manual triage workflows. Recent platform updates introduce automated token validity checks alongside REST API endpoints and webhook integrations for enterprise environments. Security engineers can now query attributed findings programmatically using specific endpoints and receive real-time notifications for newly detected leaks via the secret_scanning_public_monitoring_alert event.

Three technical details stand out. First, alert validity is continuously tracked, tagging exposures as Active, Inactive, or Unknown. Second, enterprise dashboards support advanced filtering by repository, committer, secret type, and state. Third, programmatic access via GET requests allows direct integration into custom SIEM and SOAR pipelines.

An important operational caveat remains. Dismissing or closing an alert updates its state within the enterprise dashboard exclusively. It does not trigger automatic credential revocation or remove the underlying secret from the public repository.

Programmatic triage reduces response latency, yet downstream remediation still requires explicit manual intervention from developers or security operators.

slides.title: Managing Public Secret Exposures
steps: System identifies potential leaks and runs continuous validity checks to determine if tokens remain active.
Security teams ingest findings via webhooks and REST APIs to filter and prioritize active exposures.
Operators update alert states in the dashboard while performing manual credential revocation externally.

slides.title: Enterprise Alert Management
features: Dismiss or reopen alerts directly within enterprise dashboards with optional contextual comments for team visibility.
View a complete timeline and audit trail of state changes across all monitored repositories and security teams.
Filter and sort findings by repository, committer, secret type, attribution method, and current alert state.

slides.title: APIs and Webhooks
cards: Query attributed findings programmatically using enterprise secret scanning endpoints for automated pipeline ingestion.
Leverage enterprise-level support for public monitoring alert events to deliver real-time notifications to external systems.
Feed structured data directly into custom security operations and incident response tools for faster triage.
